POC summary & qualitative notes:
- Use-case: automated agent that summarizes suspicious transactions into a strict JSON schema + calls an internal fraud scoring tool (tool-calling).
- During POC Redwood produced lower pass-rate on schema validation (4.2% more post-processing required) vs Anthropic baseline; ML team reported more brittle tool-call triggers.
- SE (Maya) pushed quantization/profile adjustments and deterministic sampling settings; marginal improvement but not enough to close gap.
- InfoSec: heavy focus on data residency and KMS integration; Redwood's private demo looked promising but attestation timeline unclear.
- Commercial: ARR estimate conservative (50k-150k) but procurement froze after Head of ML Ops left.
- Sales touches: multiple short emails in Dec/Jan, low replies after 2026-01-18.
- Direct quote from Head of Product during final eval: 'We can't introduce regressions to our fraud workflows, even if cheaper.'
- Action: Archive; keep security artifacts on file and watch for champion return or Anthropic regression.
- Links: pricing deck and security checklist attached to opportunity folder.
